status: FROZEN before any request or scoring; approved by the owner on 2026-10-16
role: run D of docs/HANDOFF.md: replicate, on more models and a second same-domain split, the finding that retrieving in-scope examples suppresses a general model's rejection of same-domain unsupported requests, and test two mitigations
claim_under_test: Adding retrieved in-scope examples to the prompt lowers the share of held-out-intent (same-domain, unsupported) requests the general model rejects, compared with the same model zero-shot.
prior_evidence: Exploratory, on the old 400 BANKING77-OOS 'id' sessions: Gemma 4 31B rejected 69.6% of held-out-intent turns zero-shot and 37.7% with retrieval; Qwen3.5 27B 88.4% and 66.6%. The confirmatory run (docs/confirmatory-results.md) showed the same pattern for whole held-out MASSIVE domains: Gemma with in-scope retrieval caught 23.0% of them, and 90.5% when labelled out-of-scope rows were in the pool. Written after seeing those numbers, before any request below.

banking77_oos.in_scope_items: the 398 in-scope test utterances not used in the earlier 'id' sessions (45 of 50 intents)
banking77_oos.held_out_items: the 679 id-oos test utterances (27 held-out Banking77 intents) not used in the earlier 'id' sessions
banking77_oos.held_out_intent_names: data/banking77-oos/id-oos/test/label_original, downloaded 2026-10-16 with the owner's permission from the same repository and commit (fa955331); its seq.in matches the local file byte for byte

clinc_single_domain.source: data/clinc-single-domain-oos, commit fa955331 (downloaded 2026-10-15 with the owner's permission)

domains.banking: 10 in-scope intents; 500 in-scope test and 350 id-oos test utterances (5 held-out banking intents)
domains.credit_cards: 10 in-scope intents; 500 in-scope test and 350 id-oos test utterances (5 held-out credit-card intents)

clinc_single_domain.analysis: the two domains are pooled for the tests (1,000 in-scope, 700 held-out items, 10 held-out-intent clusters) and also reported separately

splits.frozen_lists: artifacts/retrieval-suppression/items.json, SHA-256 85410e0888994b8a9b53e26718246e98abde336c02e11ee1518f5e1444778aeb (banking77_oos 398 in-scope / 679 held-out, 27 held-out intents; clinc_banking and clinc_credit_cards 500 / 350 each, 5 held-out intents each)

arms.zero_shot: system prompt with the option list; user message 'Current message: {text}'
arms.retrieval: the same system prompt; user message holds the 20 BM25 nearest in-scope training utterances ('message => code', least similar first), then the current message. No out-of-scope rows.
arms.mitigation_instruction: the retrieval arm with one sentence added to the system prompt after the first paragraph: 'The labelled examples show only supported request types. A message that resembles them but asks for something none of the options covers is out of scope: answer scope: no.'
arms.mitigation_rows: the retrieval arm with four fixed out-of-scope examples always listed first, before the 20 retrieved examples, with the out-of-scope code: the first four CLINC150 out-of-scope training queries ('how much is an overdraft fee for bank', and three off-topic queries). A deployment has no examples of the intents it does not know; the first row happens to be banking-related.

prompts.banking77_oos: workflow_near_oos_protocol.json hosted.system_prompt, unchanged (it already says 'anything else, including other banking questions, must be passed on')
prompts.clinc_single_domain: the same text with 'a retail bank's customer-support desk' replaced by 'a bank's customer-support desk' (banking) or 'a credit-card support desk' (credit_cards), and 'other banking questions' by 'other banking or credit-card questions'
prompts.codes: two digits, option position from 1 in alphabetical label order; 00 = out of scope
prompts.request: temperature 0, max_tokens 24, reasoning disabled where the model has a reasoning switch, pinned host, fallbacks off; parsing by workflow_v4.parse; a failed request counts as wrong (an in-scope item rejected, a held-out item accepted)

gemma-4-31b.role: replication of the exploratory result on fresh items

qwen3.5-27b.role: replication of the exploratory result on fresh items

llama-3.3-70b.role: new: dense 70B, another family; no reasoning mode

deepseek-v4-pro.role: new: 1.6T-parameter mixture of experts (49B active), another family
deepseek-v4-pro.precision: fp8; no first-party host on OpenRouter

specialist_reference.banking77_oos: the three existing 150M Ettin specialists (revision features), prior-weighted threshold on 400 in-scope validation and 100 id-oos validation utterances, scored on the same items
specialist_reference.clinc_single_domain: three new specialists per domain (seeds 20261007, 20261015, 20261016), Program 2 recipe, learning rate 1e-4, 3 epochs, trained on the 500 in-scope training utterances; temperature and prior-weighted threshold on the 500 in-scope validation and the first 100 id-oos validation utterances
specialist_reference.note: reference only, no test against the models. The specialist's threshold sees 100 held-out-intent validation items; the general models see none. Stated as an asymmetry.

endpoints.held_out_rejected: share of held-out-intent items answered scope: no (primary)
endpoints.in_scope_right: share of in-scope items answered scope: yes with the right intent
endpoints.also: in-scope kept, intent accuracy on kept items, parse failures, tokens, USD and latency per call

primary_H1.family: 4 models x 2 splits = 8 tests, Holm, one-sided alpha 0.05
primary_H1.statistic: paired difference in held-out rejection over the same items; sign-flip test with 10,000 draws clustered by held-out intent (27 clusters on banking77_oos, 10 on clinc_single_domain); 95% cluster-bootstrap interval
primary_H1.replicates_if: on a split, the drop is significant after Holm for at least three of the four models and has the same sign for all four

secondary_H2_mitigation.hypothesis: held_out_rejected(mitigation) > held_out_rejected(retrieval), for each mitigation arm
secondary_H2_mitigation.family: 4 models x 2 splits x 2 arms = 16 tests, Holm, one-sided
secondary_H2_mitigation.works_if: for a model and split, the mitigation recovers at least half of the suppression (rejection >= retrieval + 0.5 x (zero_shot - retrieval)) and in_scope_right falls by no more than 2 points against retrieval (cluster-bootstrap 95% interval of the in-scope change above -2 points)

tests.also_reported: in-scope right per arm with intervals; the specialist reference; each CLINC domain separately

outcome_sentences.replicates: Retrieving in-scope examples lowers the rejection of same-domain unsupported requests for {k} of 4 general models on {split} (by {range} points).
outcome_sentences.does_not_replicate: On {split}, retrieval lowers the rejection of same-domain unsupported requests for only {k} of 4 models; the suppression is not general.
outcome_sentences.mitigation_works: {arm} recovers {share}% of the lost rejections for {model} on {split} at a cost of {d} points of in-scope accuracy.
outcome_sentences.mitigation_fails: Neither mitigation recovers half of the suppression without costing more than 2 points of in-scope accuracy.

check.what: 5 in-scope and 5 held-out validation items per model, split and arm; not reported

D.what: 4 models x 4 arms x 2,777 items = 44,432 calls

runs.estimate_basis: measured per-call cost of the earlier BANKING77-OOS zero-shot and retrieval runs (Gemma 0.078e-3 and 0.131e-3 USD; Qwen 0.116e-3 and 0.189e-3) scaled by each model's input price and each split's prompt length (CLINC single-domain prompts list 10 options, so they are about half as long)
runs.order: check; then models cheapest first (llama, gemma, qwen, deepseek); within a model all arms of a split together

limits: Two benchmarks built by one group; held-out intents are chosen by the benchmark authors. Fixed seeds, temperature 0, one run per model. The mitigation rows are off-topic examples.
code: src/bakeoff/retrieval_suppression.py (stages build, train, check, hosted, analyze); runner scripts/run_retrieval_suppression.sh
notes: CLINC single-domain test utterances are used exactly as released, including stray quote characters in a few of them.
